vars.label: Broadband serviceable locations (FCC)
vars.ref: FCC Broadband Data Collection, fixed broadband availability, Puerto Rico state location files, releases as of June 30 of 2023-2026 (newest as of 2026-06-30); tiers as NTIA's BEAD program defines them
vars.definition: The number of broadband serviceable locations in the area. A broadband serviceable location is a place where the FCC's list (the Fabric) says a home or business is or could be served: a house, an apartment building, a business. Availability is what providers report they can install within ten business days, not what anyone subscribes to or the speed anyone gets. Each year's value is the release as of June 30 of that year. Each location belongs to its 2020 census block.

vars.label: Locations served at 100/20 Mbps or more (FCC, %)
vars.ref: FCC Broadband Data Collection, fixed broadband availability, Puerto Rico state location files, releases as of June 30 of 2023-2026 (newest as of 2026-06-30); tiers as NTIA's BEAD program defines them
vars.definition: The share of the area's locations that can get 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload or more over a reliable technology: 'served' in NTIA's BEAD terms. Reliable technologies are copper, cable, fiber to the premises and licensed or licensed-by-rule fixed wireless, with low latency (100 ms or less); satellite and unlicensed fixed wireless do not count (NTIA's BEAD rules). A broadband serviceable location is a place where the FCC's list (the Fabric) says a home or business is or could be served: a house, an apartment building, a business. Availability is what providers report they can install within ten business days, not what anyone subscribes to or the speed anyone gets. Each year's value is the release as of June 30 of that year. Each location belongs to its 2020 census block.

vars.label: Locations underserved, 25/3 to 100/20 Mbps (FCC, %)
vars.ref: FCC Broadband Data Collection, fixed broadband availability, Puerto Rico state location files, releases as of June 30 of 2023-2026 (newest as of 2026-06-30); tiers as NTIA's BEAD program defines them
vars.definition: The share of the area's locations whose best service over a reliable technology is at least 25/3 Mbps but less than 100/20: 'underserved' in NTIA's BEAD terms. Reliable technologies are copper, cable, fiber to the premises and licensed or licensed-by-rule fixed wireless, with low latency (100 ms or less); satellite and unlicensed fixed wireless do not count (NTIA's BEAD rules). A broadband serviceable location is a place where the FCC's list (the Fabric) says a home or business is or could be served: a house, an apartment building, a business. Availability is what providers report they can install within ten business days, not what anyone subscribes to or the speed anyone gets. Each year's value is the release as of June 30 of that year. Each location belongs to its 2020 census block.

vars.ref: FCC Broadband Data Collection, fixed broadband availability, Puerto Rico state location files, releases as of June 30 of 2023-2026 (newest as of 2026-06-30); tiers as NTIA's BEAD program defines them
vars.definition: The share of the area's locations with no service of 25/3 Mbps or more over a reliable technology (they may still have satellite or unlicensed fixed wireless): 'unserved' in NTIA's BEAD terms. Reliable technologies are copper, cable, fiber to the premises and licensed or licensed-by-rule fixed wireless, with low latency (100 ms or less); satellite and unlicensed fixed wireless do not count (NTIA's BEAD rules). A broadband serviceable location is a place where the FCC's list (the Fabric) says a home or business is or could be served: a house, an apartment building, a business. Availability is what providers report they can install within ten business days, not what anyone subscribes to or the speed anyone gets. Each year's value is the release as of June 30 of that year. Each location belongs to its 2020 census block.

vars.label: Locations below 100/20 Mbps, underserved or unserved (FCC)
vars.ref: FCC Broadband Data Collection, fixed broadband availability, Puerto Rico state location files, releases as of June 30 of 2023-2026 (newest as of 2026-06-30); tiers as NTIA's BEAD program defines them
vars.definition: The number of the area's locations that are underserved or unserved: those that cannot get 100/20 Mbps over a reliable technology (the locations NTIA's BEAD program can fund). Reliable technologies are copper, cable, fiber to the premises and licensed or licensed-by-rule fixed wireless, with low latency (100 ms or less); satellite and unlicensed fixed wireless do not count (NTIA's BEAD rules). A broadband serviceable location is a place where the FCC's list (the Fabric) says a home or business is or could be served: a house, an apartment building, a business. Availability is what providers report they can install within ten business days, not what anyone subscribes to or the speed anyone gets. Each year's value is the release as of June 30 of that year. Each location belongs to its 2020 census block.

vars.label: Locations where fiber is available (FCC, %)
vars.ref: FCC Broadband Data Collection, fixed broadband availability, Puerto Rico state location files, releases as of June 30 of 2023-2026 (newest as of 2026-06-30); tiers as NTIA's BEAD program defines them
vars.definition: The share of the area's locations where at least one provider reports fiber to the premises, at any speed. A broadband serviceable location is a place where the FCC's list (the Fabric) says a home or business is or could be served: a house, an apartment building, a business. Availability is what providers report they can install within ten business days, not what anyone subscribes to or the speed anyone gets. Each year's value is the release as of June 30 of that year. Each location belongs to its 2020 census block.
